title: Dubai App Development: 38 of 62 Clutch Firms List $25 to $49
desc: Most first-page Clutch app agencies in Dubai list $25 to $99 an hour and a $10,000+ minimum. Plus 5% VAT if registered, store fees, commission and UAE data law.
keywords: app development dubai, mobile app development dubai, app development company dubai, app developer dubai, app development cost dubai, app development uae, mobile app development cost uae
cta: Want a scoped quote for your app in Dubai?
body:
Short answer. On the first page of Clutch's Dubai app developer directory, 38 of the 62 firms list $25 to $49 an hour, and 55 of 62 sit between $25 and $99. Two thirds (42 of 62) list a minimum project of $10,000 or more. A VAT-registered UAE agency then adds 5% VAT, and you pay Apple 99 USD a year and Google Play US$25 once to publish. We read every source below on 11 November 2026.

This guide is for a founder or a business in the UAE that wants an iOS or Android app built by a Dubai agency. It covers what agencies list, what a build adds up to, the VAT rule, the store accounts, what Apple and Google keep from sales, and the UAE data law your app has to follow. If you are still choosing between a freelancer, an agency and an in-house hire, start with our guide to hiring an app developer.

What Dubai app agencies list on Clutch

Clutch's Top App Developers in Dubai page counted 937 companies when we read it, with ratings marked as updated on November 11, 2026. Each firm card shows a listed hourly rate band and a minimum project size. We counted the first page in the default sort: 80 cards, which reduce to 62 different firms because featured placements repeat. All 62 list a UAE location, 57 of them in Dubai.

One caution before the numbers. Clutch says plainly that it "may earn a fee for some placements", the first page includes featured placements, and it is a sample of the 937, not all of them. Clutch does not publish an average Dubai project cost on the page.

Listed hourly rateFirms on page oneShare
Under $2569.7%
$25 to $493861.3%
$50 to $991727.4%
$300 or more11.6%

Minimum project sizes on the same 62 firms: 5 list $1,000+, 13 list $5,000+, 20 list $10,000+, 17 list $25,000+, 4 list $50,000+, 1 lists $250,000+ and 2 do not disclose one. So 42 of 62, about 68%, list a minimum project of $10,000 or more.

Dubai rates next to the global Clutch directory

We counted Clutch's worldwide mobile app development directory the same morning, again on the first page in the default sort. The two pages are snapshots, not surveys, but they differ.

BandDubai page (62 firms)Global page (66 firms)
Under $25 an hour6 (9.7%)9 (13.6%)
$25 to $99 an hour55 (88.7%)43 (65.2%)
$100 an hour or more1 (1.6%)14 (21.2%)

The Dubai first page is bunched in the $25 to $99 middle, with almost no firms listing $100 or more. In our view that means a Dubai quote far above $99 an hour deserves a question about why, and a quote far below $25 deserves a question about who does the work.

A 400-hour build at Dubai agency rates

Cost is hours times rate, so the hour count matters. The example below is hypothetical: a 400-hour first version, priced at the edges of the two bands most first-page Dubai firms list. Your scope sets the real hours; our app development cost guide covers how features change them.

Listed band400 hours at the low end400 hours at the high end5% VAT on the high end
$25 to $49 an hour$10,000$19,600$980
$50 to $99 an hour$20,000$39,600$1,980

Add 99 USD for the first Apple membership year and US$25 for Google Play, which is $124 in year one before any design, hosting or maintenance costs. The hourly figures are listed bands, not quotes.

When 5% VAT goes on the invoice

The UAE government portal's VAT page says VAT "was introduced in the UAE on 1 January 2018" and "the rate of VAT is 5 per cent". Registration is mandatory when "the taxable supplies and imports of a UAE-based business exceed AED 375,000 per annum", and optional above AED 187,500. Registered businesses "must charge VAT on taxable goods or services they supply" and "may reclaim any VAT they have paid on business-related goods or services".

In practice: if your agency is VAT-registered, expect 5% on top of its quote. If your own company is VAT-registered and the app is for the business, the same page says you may reclaim VAT paid on business-related services, so you may be able to reclaim the 5%. Ask every agency whether its quote includes VAT. This is general information, not tax advice.

App Store and Google Play accounts for a UAE business

Apple says the Apple Developer Program "is 99 USD per membership year, or in local currency where available". Google Play charges a US$25 one-time registration fee. Both ask an organization for a D-U-N-S number (Apple, Google), and Apple shows "your organization's name" as the seller on the App Store.

Two practical points for a Dubai build. First, open the accounts in your company's name, not the agency's; our guide on who should own your app store account explains why. Second, if you use a personal Google Play account created after November 13, 2023, Google requires a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in continuously for at least 14 days before the app is eligible for distribution, so plan at least two weeks.

What Apple and Google keep from UAE sales

If the app is paid or sells in-app purchases or subscriptions, the stores take a share. Apple's Small Business Program offers "a reduced commission rate of 15% on paid apps and Apple In-App Purchases" to developers who qualify: those new to the App Store or with up to 1 million USD in proceeds in the prior calendar year. Above 1 million USD in the current year, Apple says the standard rate applies to future sales.

Google's service fee page lists a new fee structure only for users in Australia, the EEA, Japan, the UK and the US. The UAE is not on that list, so by our reading UAE sales fall under "all remaining markets" until Google rolls out its updated fees globally: 15% on the first $1M of revenue each year for developers enrolled in the 15% tier, 30% above that, and 15% on auto-renewing subscriptions. On a hypothetical $10,000 of in-app sales at a 15% rate, $1,500 goes to the store.

The UAE data law to know

Many apps collect personal data, such as a phone number, a location or a payment record. The UAE portal's data protection page describes Federal Decree Law No. 45 of 2021, the Personal Data Protection Law, which "came into force on 2 January 2022". It says the law "prohibits the processing of personal data without the consent of its owner", with exceptions such as protecting a public interest or carrying out legal procedures. It gives people "the right to request for corrections of inaccurate personal data and to restrict or stop the processing", and it "sets out the requirements for the cross-border transfer" of data.

The same page lists other rules an app may meet: a separate Data Protection Law, DIFC Law No 5 of 2020, and Federal Law No. 2 of 2019 for information technology in health care, "including its free zones". Ask your agency where user data will be stored, how consent is collected in the app, and how a user can ask for a correction. This is general information, not legal advice.

Arabic and right-to-left layouts

If your users read Arabic, Apple's Human Interface Guidelines say to "support right-to-left languages like Arabic and Hebrew by reversing your interface as needed", and that system UI frameworks "support right-to-left (RTL) by default". We suggest you ask the agency to show an Arabic build of one real screen before you sign, not only English mockups.

For scale, Kepios counted 23.0 million cellular mobile connections in the UAE in late 2025, equal to 202 percent of the population; it notes some of these may be data-only or secondary connections.

How to compare Dubai app agencies

These are our suggestions, built from the numbers above:

  • Ask for a quote in hours and rate, not only a total, so you can place it against the $25 to $99 bands.
  • Check the minimum project size first. Two thirds of the first-page firms list $10,000 or more.
  • Ask whether VAT is included and whether the agency is VAT-registered.
  • Confirm the App Store and Google Play accounts will be in your company's name.
  • Ask how the app collects consent and where the data lives under the UAE data law.
  • See a working Arabic screen if your users read Arabic.

faqs: How much does app development cost in Dubai?

On the first page of Clutch's Dubai directory, read 11 November 2026, 55 of 62 firms list $25 to $99 an hour and 42 of 62 list a minimum project of $10,000 or more. A hypothetical 400-hour build comes to $10,000 to $39,600 across those bands, before 5% VAT from a VAT-registered agency.
What is the hourly rate of app developers in Dubai?
38 of the 62 firms on Clutch's Dubai first page list $25 to $49 an hour, 17 list $50 to $99, 6 list under $25 and 1 lists $300 or more. These are listed bands, not quotes.
Do Dubai app agencies charge VAT?

A VAT-registered UAE business generally must charge 5% VAT on taxable services. Registration is mandatory above AED 375,000 of taxable supplies and imports a year, so ask each agency whether its quote includes VAT.
How much does it cost to put an app on the App Store and Google Play from the UAE?

Apple charges 99 USD per membership year, or local currency where available, and Google Play charges a US$25 one-time registration fee. That is $124 in year one, and both ask an organization for a D-U-N-S number.
How much do Apple and Google take from app sales in the UAE?

Developers who qualify for and join Apple's Small Business Program (new to the App Store, or up to 1 million USD in prior-year proceeds) pay 15%. For markets outside its new fee list, Google Play lists 15% on the first $1M a year in its 15% tier and 30% above that, until it rolls out updated fees globally.
Which UAE law covers personal data in an app?

Federal Decree Law No. 45 of 2021, the Personal Data Protection Law, in force since 2 January 2022. The UAE portal says it bars processing personal data without consent except in listed cases and sets rules for cross-border transfers. This is general information, not legal advice.
